title: December 15 keeps the quarter-percent guide ahead of year-end
summary: A majority retained the average unsecured overnight call rate guide around 0.25 percent. It remained the guideline for the intermeeting period. The release specifies no year-end liquidity operation and offers no numerical path for the following year. The target can be used to benchmark overnight outcomes, while the price of borrowing across the year-end boundary is a separate market observation.

The meeting ended at 2:31 p.m. Deputy Governor Fujiwara chaired during Governor Hayami’s temporary absence earlier in the morning. The Bank scheduled the economic view for December 18, the English background within a few business days of that release, and the minutes for January 24, 2001.

questions.question: Was any turn-of-year funding premium confined to contracts crossing year-end?
questions.detail: Compare rates on otherwise similar instruments with different settlements around December 31. Match maturities and credit exposure before linking a premium to year-end demand.

questions.question: Did any change in the expected path survive the economic report?
questions.detail: Compare the curve immediately after the decision and around the December 18 publication. The two windows distinguish news about the rate setting from the later economic assessment.

questions.question: How should simultaneous publication of meeting records be handled?
questions.detail: Check the January 24 release list and timestamp each record. If several were made available together, prices can identify only the combined information in that publication window.
